content:
kevin (stripe-payments): Hey, getting a flood of 429s from our integration starting at ~02:15 UTC. Happens when our nightly order-sync job runs, previously fine. No code changes on our side.

alisha (support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste one of the failing request IDs or the response headers you see? 429 body?

kevin (stripe-payments): sample headers from the client: `Retry-After: 30`, `x-rate-limit-limit: 120 rpm`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 1712004300`. Body is just `\{\"error\":\"rate limit exceeded\"\}`. Request id: req_01GZz8XYZ

alisha (support): thanks. that limit looks like per-minute (rpm) — are you doing parallel calls from multiple hosts? any fan-out?

kevin (stripe-payments): yeah we have 8 worker pods all starting the job at same time. Each does ~200 small requests (not batching) over ~2 minutes. We've surfaced the 429s to Sentry but that's it.

maya (eng-platform): tagging in to confirm: the headers look like the hosted API RPM window. When many clients start concurrently you can hit burst/exhaustion even if overall throughput is okay. Any chance the SDK's retries are disabled? that can amplify spikes.

jordan (sre): quick checklist for repro: 1) cron across 8 pods start at same time 2) each pod sends 200 sequential requests with concurrency 10 3) no client-side backoff 4) per-account quota 120 rpm. if so, math: 8 pods * 200 reqs ~1600 reqs, even spread over 2 minutes that's 800 rpm -> well over 120 rpm.

kevin (stripe-payments): ugh, ok that makes sense. I can change the cron but need immediate mitigation. Any quick config to reduce failures?

alisha (support): immediate mitigations: 1) add jitter to cron start (stagger pods) 2) reduce client concurrency to 2-4 while we triage 3) implement exponential backoff on 429s with jitter (example below) 4) batch small operations into single request if possible.

alisha (support): example backoff pattern we recommend:
```
retry_count = 0
while retry_count < 6:
  wait = min(60, (2 ** retry_count) + random() * 0.5)
  sleep(wait)
  retry_request()
  retry_count += 1
```
Also honor `Retry-After` header if present (use that value, then apply jitter).

kevin (stripe-payments): can you also check server-side whether those 429s were per-minute quota or token-per-minute? we use both per-account rate limits and plan-level quotas.

maya (eng-platform): looking now — ops bot shows an alert spike at 02:15 with rate limit key `acct_98az` hitting limit. Logs show `limit_type: rpm`, and bucket reset timestamps match header. Also see `burst_window: 30s` configured for that plan.

devops-bot: Incident alert: high 429 rate for acct_98az between 1742003650 - 1742003720. Peak 429ps=45.

jordan (sre): two routes forward: A) short term: support can apply a temporary burst increase (raises rpm for next 24h) while customer staggers job B) long term: migrate heavy jobs to Dedicated or request a quota bump and redesign client to batch/persist and use token bucket.

alisha (support): Kevin, would you like us to request a temporary burst increase? it requires confirmation you will adjust cron to remove the simultaneous fan-out within 24h.

kevin (stripe-payments): yes please. we'll stagger starts and add backoff. also any quick tip to detect this pattern automatically?

maya (eng-platform): enable per-route token accounting in the console and set an alert where `x-rate-limit-remaining < 10` AND `429_count > 5` over 1m. That will catch imminent exhaustion. Also use the SDK's built-in token-bucket helper (we have example in devex).

alisha (support): I've initiated a temporary +2x burst for 24h for acct_98az. Ops will monitor. Please send updated repro steps once you stagger the cron.

ops-oncall: applied temporary quota change: old=120rpm new=240rpm (expires in 24h). Monitoring for error reduction.

kevin (stripe-payments): got it — cron staggered across 8 pods by adding random 0-90s sleep, concurrency down to 3, added retries w/jitter. We'll report back in morning. Thanks. :pray: 

maya (eng-platform): follow-ups for engineering: 1) check whether dedicated capacity is appropriate for sustained throughput (>500 rpm) 2) investigate if we need to provide a canned client-side rate-limiter snippet for common languages 3) confirm our docs show clear math examples for fan-out scenarios.

jordan (sre): note for postmortem: root cause = synchronized nightly fan-out + lack of client-side rate limiting. Mitigation applied = temporary quota increase + customer stagger/backoff. Recommend adding a KB article.

alisha (support): Kevin — we'll keep monitoring for the next 6 hours and confirm closure if 429s stop. Feel free to DM me request IDs if you see new ones.

kevin (stripe-payments): will do. appreciate the fast help.

devops-bot: Alert resolved: 429 rate returned to baseline for acct_98az (last 30m).

alisha (support): closing loop — resolved for now. documenting KB with suggested client patterns, example code, and quota escalation path.

kevin (stripe-payments): thanks all!
